projects.title: GateOrchestra
projects.description: A lightweight, trainable gate that sits in front of a multi-agent orchestrator. Using only pre-execution signals, it decides whether a cheap single-agent probe answer is good enough or whether the full multi-agent system is worth its tokens. Built with a four-person team.
highlights: 33% fewer tokens than always running the multi-agent system, at higher accuracy (97.9% vs 92.2% on Qwen2.5-3B)
Evaluated on 96 held-out tasks across two seeds, under equal token budgets

projects.title: Autonomous Orchestrator Agent
projects.description: An audited multi-agent orchestration service. Plain-language instructions are routed across a nine-agent roster, with a human approval gate in front of anything outbound, a crash-resilient autonomy engine, sandboxed web browsing and multi-tier memory.
highlights: HMAC-signed human-in-the-loop approval gate that cannot be bypassed
239 passing tests and a 100% score on the router evaluation harness

projects.title: Self-Improving Code Agent
projects.description: A sandboxed, self-repairing coding agent. It runs untrusted Python inside isolated Docker containers, reads its own tracebacks to repair bugs, remembers failure patterns in ChromaDB vector memory, and audits the result through multi-agent review.
highlights: Spec tests are written first; every step streams live over server-sent events
Verified runs earn a certificate: tests, coverage, security findings and complexity

projects.title: NebulaLM
projects.description: A decoder-only language model for space and astronomy, built from scratch, and a pre-registered study of what a 4.5M–29M parameter model learns, stores and leaks as it trains on repeated text.
highlights: The 29.4M model reaches 1.060 bits per byte on the sealed test split — 23% below a 5-gram baseline
Verbatim extraction stays under 1%; rejected hypotheses are reported as rejected

screenshot.alt: NebulaLM — a small astronomy language model and a study of what it learns, stores and leaks
screenshot.caption: NebulaLM — research presentation title slide

projects.title: Visentra
projects.description: A forensic workstation for computer-vision supply chains. It ties cryptographic provenance — hashes, Merkle roots and Ed25519 signatures — to behavioural checks on one live lineage graph, so a poisoned sample, a flipped weight bit or a planted backdoor all surface in the same place.
highlights: Four pillars: dataset integrity, model integrity, backdoor screening and inference binding
Every prediction downstream of a tampered artefact loses its certificate

more.title: CrisisRoute
more.description: Decision support for post-disaster relief logistics. It estimates how likely each road is to be passable, plans which depots and vehicles serve which communities, and requires a second person to sign off every plan.

more.title: PatchGraph
more.description: Explainable, constrained supply-chain remediation — “patch what matters.” It explains and recommends but never patches automatically; every decision needs human approval and is sealed into an append-only audit log.

more.title: AquaSphere
more.description: A satellite-embedding deep learning system that reconstructs subsurface ocean temperature profiles (0–1000 m) from surface satellite data, validated against real ARGO float observations for the North Indian Ocean.

more.title: GenAI Lab

more.title: InterviewPro
more.description: AI-powered interview preparation platform using the Claude API — generates role-specific interview questions and delivers structured feedback on user responses in real time.
